A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiT and provide readable main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The reorganized material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet experiments, architectural and training ablations, latency measurements, and generated text-to-image samples.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and additionally reports GenEval evaluation, text-to-image latency comparisons, and an implementation ablation.

M1.justification: The five guidelines retain the same ReLU linear attention with depth-wise convolution, few heads, selective weight inheritance, and noise-plus-variance distillation. Figure 3 and the objectives remain equivalent. The added implementation discussion and pseudocode precision refinements do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds systematic GenEval coverage at 512px and 1024px, evaluating single/two objects, counting, colors, positions, and attributes. This substantially extends text-to-image evaluation beyond v1's selected qualitative examples. ImageNet coverage remains unchanged.

E2.justification: New Table 8 compares LiT with LDM, SDv1.5, SDv2.1, LlamaGen, PixArt-α, PixArt-Σ, Lumina-Next, SEED-X, Chameleon, and LWM; Table 9 adds a direct PixArt-Σ latency comparison. ImageNet comparators remain unchanged. Table 5 corrects v1's repeated DiG-S/2 labels to the corresponding S/B/L/XL variants without changing their scores.

E3.justification: Reported 512px text-to-image training changes from 45,400 to approximately 106K steps, with token length now 300 rather than the earlier 120. The four-stage 1K description, with batches 64/64/256/256, becomes approximately 155K continuation steps at batch 2×48. New GenEval evaluation and batch-one, 20-step latency measurements extend the protocol. These reported revisions do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: A new footnote in v2 Section 3.1 tests attention without the stated implementation optimizations, reporting S/2 and B/2 FIDs of 63.13 and 42.13 versus 63.66 and 42.11. Existing head-count, inheritance, and distillation ablations remain unchanged. The attention-head similarity analysis is relocated to the appendix.

E5.justification: v2 specifies averaging over 10 runs for the new PixArt-Σ latency comparison. Existing head-count latency studies retain their 30-repeat reporting. Neither version provides confidence intervals or significance tests for generation-quality comparisons.

E6.justification: New Table 8 reports LiT GenEval overall scores of 0.47 at 512px and 0.48 at 1024px, versus PixArt-Σ's 0.52. Table 9 reports LiT/PixArt-Σ latency of 3.93/4.38 seconds at 1K and 14.59/32.16 seconds at 2K. These are newly reported comparisons; existing ImageNet tables and corresponding appendix scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The diffusion formulation, linear-attention equations, computational-complexity expressions, and distillation objectives remain equivalent. v2 adds explanatory discussion of attention rank and locality, but no new formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: v2 emphasizes converting pretrained DiT/PixArt-Σ models without a performance gap and adds a claim of comparable GenEval performance. The underlying five contributions remain. Its abstract changes the claimed 512px training fraction from approximately 23% to 33%, although Section 4.1 still reports 700K versus 3M steps.

C2.justification: v2 expands the mechanism explanation by linking depth-wise convolution to low-rank attention and feature diversity. It interprets the new GenEval results as competitive with PixArt-Σ and discusses efficiency relative to key-value compression. Existing interpretations of head redundancy, weight transfer, and distillation largely remain, as does the unresolved 4K-generation boundary.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents 250 ImageNet sampling steps, 20 text-to-image sampling steps, and a 512px training batch of 8×48. Algorithm 1 adds an explicit fp32_attention setting and an fp16 cast before projection. Conversely, v1's project-page link and disclosure of 32 V100 GPUs for 1K training are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds CLEAR and the deep compression autoencoder to its discussion of alternative architectural choices, alongside references supporting GenEval and its new comparators. Positioning shifts toward simple conversion of pretrained models. Some background citations disappear, but the extensive appendix survey and most relationships to prior work remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, motivation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten around pretrained-model conversion. The standalone main-text related-work section disappears while the appendix survey remains, deployment is incorporated into text-to-image experiments, and appendix sections are reorganized. The title changes from 'Simplified' to 'Simple'.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 8–9 and the weight-inheritance schematic in Figure 6. It moves the roadmap radar to the opening page and relocates head-similarity analysis, the main 512px gallery, and deployment photographs to the appendix. The architecture-comparison panel is removed; 1K examples decrease from six to four and deployment photographs from four to two. The 512px sample images are retained.

improvement.justification: GenEval and direct PixArt-Σ timing comparisons strengthen text-to-image claims that v1 supported mainly through examples and module-level efficiency measurements. The implementation control and clearer explanations also help assessment. These gains outweigh limited reporting regressions, including the new 33%/23% training-fraction inconsistency and omitted project link. Stronger claims of conversion without a performance gap remain insufficiently established by the reported GenEval scores.
